added: Mounting an outdoor motion sensor light to your home can help you feel safer, as your outdoor space will light up whenever someone approaches your house. It can also add a layer of convenience, such as when taking out the garbage at night or fumbling with keys at the front door. Fortunately, installing a motion sensor light is a relatively simple process.

#Turn off the power to the light. Since most outdoor motion sensor lighting is installed in place of a current porch light, you will need to begin the project by removing the old light. Before you even touch the light, you want to go to your home’s electrical box and cut off the power to the existing light.<ref>https://www.lowes.com/n/how-to/install-motion-lights</ref>[[Image:Install an Outdoor Motion Sensor Light Step 1 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Remove the wire connections. You will see three separate wires attached to the light. There will be a white wire (the neutral wire), a green or copper wire (the ground wire), and a black or red wire (the hot wire).<ref>https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Eom936hTFW8</ref> Disconnect all three wires from the current light after testing to make sure they aren’t receiving any power.[[Image:Install an Outdoor Motion Sensor Light Step 3 Version 3.jpg|center]]
{{Video:Install an Outdoor Motion Sensor Light|}}

#Place the rubber gasket that comes with the light around the outside edge of the new fixture. The new light package will include a rubber gasket that fits tightly against the base of the fixture where it attaches to the wall. Slip this gasket over the wiring on the light and into place. It doesn’t have to be perfectly aligned just yet; you just need the gasket in place before you connect the wiring on the light to the electrical box, otherwise you’ll have to disconnect it again.<ref>https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Eom936hTFW8</ref>[[Image:Install an Outdoor Motion Sensor Light Step 6 Version 3.jpg|center]]

#Screw the light assembly into the electrical box bracket with the gasket in place. Once the wiring is all connected and taped off, you can simply push the wiring into the electrical box to give yourself more room to fit the light assembly on the wall. Your particular setup will likely have one or two screws that you use to attach the light to the cross bracket that you already attached. It can also add a layer of convenience, such as when taking out the garbage at night or fumbling with keys at the front door. Fortunately, installing a motion sensor light is a relatively simple process.
== Steps ==
=== Removing the Old Light ===

# Turn off the power to the light. Since most outdoor motion sensor lighting is installed in place of a current porch light, you will need to begin the project by removing the old light. Before you even touch the light, you want to go to your home’s electrical box and cut off the power to the existing light.<ref>http://www.lowes.com/projects/repair-and-maintain/install-motion-lights/project</ref>[[Image:Install an Outdoor Motion Sensor Light Step 2 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#* To be doubly safe, have a wire tester handy and test the wires connected to the old light to ensure no power is running to them before you actually touch them.<ref>https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Eom936hTFW8</ref>

# Remove the wire connections. You will see three separate wires attached to the light. There will be a white wire (the neutral wire), a green or copper wire (the ground wire), and a black or red wire (the hot wire).<ref>https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Eom936hTFW8</ref> Disconnect all three wires from the current light after testing to make sure they aren’t receiving any power.
#* Occasionally, especially on older homes, the hot wire may be a color other than black or red such as yellow.<ref>https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Eom936hTFW8</ref>

# Check the current electrical box. If the current light fixture is especially old, you may want to use having the light off as an excuse to change out the electrical box housing the wiring. This is especially true is you see any evidence of moisture or degraded seals around the box. The box will simply be screwed into place, and you can remove it and feed the same wiring into a new box before screwing it back into place.
=== Installing Your Motion Sensor Light ===

# Mount the adjustable crosspiece from the light package to the electrical box. The motion sensor light kit you purchase will come with a small crosspiece bracket with several different holes, allowing you to attach it to electrical boxes of different sizes.<ref>https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Eom936hTFW8</ref> Line up the bracket according to the electrical box you have installed and screw the bracket into place.

Having motion sensor lights can add a measure of safety and protection to any house. These lights can illuminate your yard and door when you come home at night and can be deterrents for would-be intruders. This article will tell you how to install an outdoor motion-sensor light.
== Steps ==
# Turn off power to the circuit you will be connecting into.
# Use a utility knife or holesaw to cut a hole in your wall for an interior light switch. Use fish tape to pull a cable from your fuse or circuit box though into your switch box.
# Fasten the box to the wall with the screws included with the unit. Secure the cable as needed with internal clamps.
# Using your knife or holesaw, make a hole where you want the motion light. The hole should be large enough for a cable clamp to be attached after fishing.
#* Pull the cable wires from the inside control to the external hole. Attach your cable clamp and pull the cable into the box. Remember to check how secure your clamp is.
# Hold the fixture on the wall and screw it onto the side of your house.
# Go back inside. Match the colors of the wires and squish them together accordingly. Remember that white is neutral and black is hot.
# Connect the dark wires to the two screws.
#* Ground your copper wires as needed.
# Assemble your light fixture and its wiring according to the item's box. Each brand is slightly different, so precisely follow the assembly and wiring directions included with the light.
#* Install a waterproofing gasket around the fixture before splicing your wires and mounting.
# Tuck all the wires into the fixture box, being sure not to bend them too much.
# Mount your fixture to the wall and use screws to attach the two pieces together. Place the durable seals over each bulb socket. Install light bulbs in each socket.
# Turn on the power and check if your switch controls the lights. When its dark out, go out and walk by the motion light to be sure the sensor is working.
== Warnings ==
* Always turn off the power while you're working. Electrical shock can occur if the power is not off.

* If you notice anything unusual in the wires in your electrical box or inside your walls (such as burned or uncoated wires), contact a certified electrician immediately. Do not proceed until the electrician has inspected and repaired damaged wires.
== Things You'll Need ==
* Insulated screwdrivers
* Utility knife or hole saw
* 6-in- tool
* Fish tape
* Correct gauge cable
* Indoor switch box and switch (if not included with motion light)
* Wire and cable connectors
* Electrical tape
* Motion-sensor outdoor light fixture, external box and mount (sometimes all included)
* Caulk and caulk gun
* Ladder
